title: Make Action View subscribers ractor safe
body:
### Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because root assignment in `ActionView::StructuredEventSubscriber` and `ActionView::LogSubscriber` ractor safe.

### Detail

This Pull Request changes log subscribers to not lazily memoize `Rails.root`. Instead, roots are set at initialize time. Similar to https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/58467.

### Additional information

The application should be making the root ractor safe / frozen, so referencing the root ivar should work on non-main ractors. Initializers will run on the main ractor for the initial assignment.

title: Fix VideoAnalyzer height precision for inexact display aspect ratios
body:
### Motivation / Background

Fixes #53538.

`ActiveStorage::Analyzer::VideoAnalyzer` derives a video's height by multiplying the encoded width by a float division of the display aspect ratio:

```ruby
Float(display_aspect_ratio.last) / display_aspect_ratio.first
```

When that ratio cannot be represented exactly in binary floating point, the height comes back slightly wrong. A 468x60 video reports a display aspect ratio of `39:5` and is analyzed as `59.99999999999999` rather than `60`, so `metadata[:height].to_i` truncates the stored height to `59`. A 970x250 video (`97:25`) is analyzed as `249.99999999999997`.

Because `width` also falls back to `computed_height` for rotated videos, the same imprecision affects the width of rotated uploads.

### Detail

The height is now computed with rational arithmetic and converted to a float once at the end, so exact ratios stay exact:

```ruby
(encoded_width.to_r * display_height_scale).to_f
```

| width | display aspect ratio | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 468 | `39:5` | `59.99999999999999` | `60.0` |
| 970 | `97:25` | `249.99999999999997` | `250.0` |
| 640 | `4:3` | `480.0` | `480.0` |
| 720 | `32:27` | `607.5` | `607.5` |

Rounding was deliberately avoided. `Float#round(0)` returns an `Integer`, which would change the documented return type of `metadata[:height]` (`{ width: 640.0, height: 480.0, ... }`), and it would also discard genuinely fractional heights such as the `607.5` above. Rational arithmetic fixes the imprecision without either side effect.

The regression test uses a new 1.9 KB fixture generated with `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i color=c=blue:s=468x60:d=1:r=10`. None of the existing video fixtures can cover this: they all have `4:3` or `16:9` ratios, which divide exactly in floating point, or no usable display aspect ratio at all.

### Additional information

[#53560](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53560) by @lmunozm1702 previously proposed a fix for this issue. A review in November 2024 asked for the unrelated style changes to be dropped and for a test case demonstrating the fix, and the pull request has been inactive since. This pull request keeps the change minimal, adds the requested regression test, and avoids the `round` behavior described above. Credit to @pozabil for the original report and diagnosis.

Verified with `BUILDKITE=1 bin/test test/analyzer/video_analyzer_test.rb` from `activestorage` (the suite's ffprobe guard otherwise skips these tests locally): 11 runs, 48 assertions, 0 failures. The new test fails with `Expected: 60 / Actual: 59.99999999999999` before the change and passes after it. RuboCop reports no offenses on the changed files.

title: delegate ActiveModel::Type::Binary::Data#as_json to its value
body:
### Motivation / Background

rails defines #as_json in most primitive objects and `ActiveModel::Type::Value`.

this does not work for binary data values however, where serialization wraps it in a `ActiveModel::Type::Binary::Data` object, which has no custom json conversion, and will therefore fallback to `Object#as_json`, which maps ivar-to-value; This does not make sense for binary data, which should just handle itself as a string.

This Pull Request has been created because I've had to monkeypatch this already a few times. It breaks particularly in situations where complex nested json objects are stored in the database using a wrapper object, such as the ones using the [store_model](https://github.com/DmitryTsepelev/store_model) gem.
